source.title: On the Dynamics & Transferability of Latent Generalization during Memorization

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no truncation indicated.
record.tranche_reason: It trains networks on randomly corrupted labels and tracks training/test accuracy, but its main measurements concern probe-based latent generalization during memorization, rather than directly testing all parts of the source claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that models were trained on 0%, 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100% label corruption, with high training accuracy (99% or 100%) as a stopping condition or a maximum of 500 epochs. Its figures plot test accuracy and corrupted-training accuracy, but do not provide direct, explicit results establishing zero training error and chance test error for each random-label setting; cited claims from Zhang et al. are not this study's results. Main extractable results are about test accuracy of MASC/VeLPIC probes and edited models. The curves are figure-only, so no precise values are inferred. The paper does not test shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, Gaussian inputs, optimizer-time multipliers, regularization removal with true-label generalization, or Arpit et al.'s pattern-before-noise claim.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own standard networks' training accuracy on corrupted labels and test accuracy on true labels, including fully random labels. These baseline measurements bear on V1 and V4; its reported early rise and later decline in model generalization also bear on V6. The extracted rows instead measure probes or weight interventions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that latent and overt generalization often rise together early, then diverge as latent generalization persists better. MASC is quadratic; VeLPIC can recover linearly decodable generalization but does not uniformly outperform MASC. Last-layer VeLPIC performance can be transferred by immediate classifier-weight editing, whereas continuing training after an epoch-40 intervention gives mixed outcomes.
record.recipe_differences: Uses standard SGD or Adam training on image datasets with randomly corrupted labels, but focuses on probe accuracy across layers and training checkpoints, and adds VeLPIC probes and pre-softmax weight editing. It does not reproduce the original papers' full set of random-label, unstructured-input, and regularization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Model architecture and layer affect probe accuracy; corruption degree affects the reported dynamics; dropout changes some MASC layer dynamics, with no significant difference reported for ResNet-18; intervention outcomes vary by model and corruption degree.

fits_no_version.finding: MASC latent generalization usually rises with overt model generalization early, then declines less and remains higher in the best layers; early ResNet-18 layers can instead remain largely flat.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representations can retain decodable generalizable information after overt model generalization deteriorates during noisy-label training.

fits_no_version.finding: VeLPIC and MASC recover different amounts of latent generalization depending on architecture and layer; neither probe uniformly dominates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The measured latent generalization of memorized networks depends on the probe and representation layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing final classifier weights with VeLPIC vectors immediately improves test accuracy in many cases, but worsens ResNet-18 generalization especially at lower corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Last-layer latent generalization can sometimes be transferred to overt model predictions by editing classifier weights without further training.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropout generally leaves probe dynamics similar, with deviations in later-layer MASC dynamics for CNN-MNIST and CNN-Fashion-MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Latent-generalization dynamics are often similar with and without the tested dropout configurations.

record.problems: The paper's stated results about probe dynamics are predominantly presented as plots without numeric values in the supplied text. Training accuracy stopping is described as 99% or 100%, but specific random-label fit outcomes are not given in prose. Dropout comparisons concern probe accuracy, not the V5 claim's direct fit and true-label generalization assertions. Training runs are averaged over three runs for main dynamics; the epoch-40 intervention figures are single-run results.
record.rows_left_out: Rows on logistic-regression probe comparison, VeLPIC-vs-MASC comparison, 0% corruption, 100% corruption, epoch-40 intervention, and additional dropout-specific plot conditions are not individually extracted because they do not measure the stated versions' direct behavior, or are outside the 60-row cap. Sections 6.1–7, Figures 3–6, Figures 8–16, and Figures 21–24 contain these results. Corrupted training-accuracy plots (Figures 17–18) are not transcribed because values are figure-only and do not directly state the unmodified model's fit result in text.

untested.parts: No reported comparison establishes a small constant training-time multiplier or systematically quantifies convergence slowing with corruption.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments; the discussion explicitly identifies input corruption as unstudied.

No direct random-label training-fit comparison with versus without dropout, weight decay, or augmentation. The dropout experiments concern latent generalization, and do not establish the claimed effect of removing regularization on true-label generalization.

No separate clean-example and noisy-example fitting curves or direct comparison of real-label versus fully random-label learning mechanisms. The relevant evidence is the temporal pattern of overt model generalization.

missing.what: Separate rows for the unmodified models' early test-accuracy rise, peak, and subsequent decline. These baseline trajectories bear on V6 and must be distinguished from MASC/VeLPIC accuracy.
missing.locator: Section 4, Figure 1 model test-accuracy reference curves; Section 10 discussion

record.verdict_notes: Remove both extracted V4 limits_scope verdicts: probe differences do not qualify V4, and untested components are not evidence against it. V1/V4 baseline results are present in figures, but the supplied text extraction contains axes and captions without readable curves; the 99%/100% stopping threshold is not an achieved result because training could stop at 500 epochs. Consequently no V1/V4 verdict is justified from the available values. Their omitted training-accuracy and endpoint results are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not duplicated in missing. V6 support concerns the reported temporal generalization pattern and does not establish separate clean/noisy-example fitting rates.

versions.untested_parts: The study trains with fully corrupted labels and states a 99% or 100% training-accuracy stopping condition, but gives no clear numeric or explicit textual result that each standard network reaches zero/near-zero training error with chance test error without changing architecture or hyperparameters.
No comparison of time to fit true versus random labels or convergence time by corruption fraction.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.

It tests corruption degrees from 0% to 100% and reports test-accuracy dynamics; text does not state that training accuracy remains perfect across those degrees or explicitly characterize test error as a steady rise toward chance.

Dropout is examined for probe latent-generalization dynamics, but the supplied results do not directly report whether dropout prevents fitting random labels or whether removing regularization harms true-label generalization. Weight decay and data augmentation are not tested.
No direct test of whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

relationships.condition: Standard training with nonzero label corruption below 100%, for the model-generalization trajectories described in Section 4
relationships.reason: Section 4 reports an early model test-accuracy peak followed by significant decline, consistent with learning signal before later overfitting; this verdict uses the text's baseline model results, which are missing from R1–R14, rather than their probe measurements.
relationships.display_finding: Model test accuracy peaked early and then declined significantly, consistent with signal learning followed by overfitting.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Most tested models and nonzero corruption degrees below 100%, as described in Section 4
reader_labels.reason: The paper says MASC test accuracy usually follows the model's early rise, then declines less steeply for best layers, but does not establish the version's full training-fit and steady-to-chance pattern (R1–R6, R8–R13). This only supports a qualified test-generalization dynamics observation.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The authors report flat or only slightly rising early-layer MASC accuracy and mixed VeLPIC behavior; this does not show the claimed smooth test-error progression (R7, R14).
